function: Learns secrecy-rate beamforming at a UAV base station (GNN) and UAV deployment (SAC) that uses the GNN beamformer to compute its reward (pp. 4-9).
system: UAV base station, 8 antennas, 100 m altitude; 8 single-antenna users each with one eavesdropper; 200 m x 200 m; no RIS; band not stated (p. 10).
method: GNN (5 GCN layers) trained unsupervised on a secrecy-rate loss for beamforming; soft actor-critic RL for deployment; GNN trained first, transfer learning for 12 users (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom Rician simulator, factor 10 dB, LoS path loss 30+22log(d) dB from [44]; users random in the area, eavesdropper about 20 m from each user (p. 10).
test_conditions: Trained with 8 users, 1 W, noise 1.2e-13 W; tested without retraining for 1-11 users, other powers and noise levels, and 12 users with transfer learning (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: optimization-based precoding and artificial noise [45], exhaustive search and four heuristic UAV placements. Learned: MLP beamformer (pp. 10, 11).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate (bps/Hz), training loss and reward, CDF of secrecy rate, computation time (pp. 10-12).
complexity: GNN inference O(D(K^2+KN^2)); SAC training O(F(BD(K^2+KN^2)+LM^2)); run time for 400 runs versus optimization (pp. 9, 12).
q1_support: p. 10: "The air-ground UAV communication channel is considered as Rician fading with a Rician factor of 10 dB". Not met: custom Rician simulator with a log-distance path loss from [44]; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "the proposed GNN model is trained for the case with 8 users, while the results for other scenarios are directly generalized based on the trained model without retraining"; p. 10: transfer learning from 8 to 12 users ("applying transfer learning based on the pre-trained model for 8 users").
q3_support: p. 10: "we consider the optimization-based scheme in [45]" and "we construct a conventional deep model with pure MLP structure to approximate the security beamforming"; p. 11: "achieving significantly higher secrecy rates compared to the MLP baseline across all tested scenarios", close to the optimization-based method (Fig. 9).
q4_support: p. 9: "the inference complexity becomes" O(D(K^2+KN^2)+LM^2) (K users, N antennas, D GCN layers, L SAC layers, M hidden units); p. 12: "we show the time taken for 400 runs" (Fig. 11, measured run time).
q5_support: p. 10: "the users are randomly distributed with a corresponding eavesdropper located about 20 m away". Not met: the data come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, public dataset or measured data appears in the paper.
notes: Area 6 by the specificity order because the transmitter is a UAV aerial base station and the learned beams control an aerial link (p. 3, p. 10); by function alone the work would be area 3 (secrecy-rate precoder, pp. 4-6), so the reviewer may want to confirm 6 versus 3. Secrecy-rate beamforming is read as a base station precoder design; physical-layer security is not on the excluded list of Step 1. The SAC UAV deployment is above the physical layer on its own but is learned jointly with the GNN beamformer (reward from the GNN, pp. 8-9), so the work passes above_phy. q2 counts the number of users (trained on 8, tested on 1-11 and 12 users without retraining or after transfer learning); the transmit-power and noise-power sweeps alone would not count. q3 counts the MLP as the standard learned architecture on the same problem and [45] as the non-learned baseline. No carrier frequency is stated; RIS appears only as a possible extension (p. 7).
